newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Tightened S.Korean security curbs gold smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Tightened S.Korean security curbs gold smuggling.

text.p: A security crackdown in South Korea following the shooting of a Northern defector has stemmed the flow of smuggled gold into the country, traders said on Tuesday.
"We haven't seen see any smuggled gold since Monday. It is quite unusal," a bullion dealer with Ssangyong Corp said.
On an average day, South Korea imports around 350 kg (770 lb) of gold a day. An estimated 85 percent of it is smuggled to avoid a three percent import tax and 10 percent value-added tax.
The security crackdown followed the weekend shooting of Li Il-nam, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's ex-wife, by suspected North Korean agents near Seoul.
Li, who defected to South Korea in 1982, is in a coma.

On Tuesday, Prime Minister Lee Soo-sung called for "extraordinary alertness" against North Korea following the shooting of Li and the apparent defection of a top Pyongyang official to Seoul's embassy in Beijing.
"We saw the same situation in the gold market last September when the country was in uproar over the incursion by a North Korean submarine," said a dealer with LG Metals Corp.

Other dealers said they expected South Korean firms to accelerate legal imports of gold and that supplies would be back to normal in about a week. Most of the imported gold is used to make jewellery and the rest for investment.
